{"id":"mimid-1wgh.114.14","title":"A restart loses every VTCCall: the object is in memory and nothing re-projects the call room","design":"Found 2026-11-25 building bead mimid-1wgh.129, by a test that failed for
a reason I did not expect: after a restart the agent answered "no such
call" rather than anything about epochs.

WHAT HAPPENS. A restart loses every VTCCall. Not under another id --
gone. Pinned by crates/mimid-agent/tests/vtc.rs
a_call_does_not_survive_a_restart_yet, which asserts VTCCall/get returns
an empty list and that the id the client holds names nothing.

WHY, and both halves have to be fixed or neither does:

  1. The object is in memory. crates/mimid-agent-jmap/src/persist.rs
     JmapExt::before_save keeps five types in each record's ext["jmap"]
     -- ChatContact, Chat, ChatBan, Message, ReadPosition -- and VtcCall
     is not among them. keep_objects then maps type to record with a
     hardcoded five-way match and a five-tuple, so a sixth type is not a
     one-line addition there.
  2. Nothing re-projects. project() runs over the store's Changes, and a
     restart produces no RoomAdded for a room already in state, so
     project_call_room never runs again.

NOTHING IS LOST THAT MATTERS, which is why this is a projection problem
and not a state problem: the call ROOM persists, with its parent, its
participants and its MLS group. The same test asserts that. Everything
needed to rebuild the VTCCall is on disk.

WHERE THE FIX BELONGS. AgentChat::over already calls load_records, which
is what restores the other types from ext["jmap"]. project_call_room's
own rustdoc says its id "is the same at every projection and across
restarts" -- which is true, and never used, because nothing projects it
again. So the smaller fix is probably to re-project call rooms at
load_records time rather than to add a sixth persisted type: a projection
that is already idempotent by design, run once more at open.

Check while doing it:

  - Decision mimid-1wgh.119: with [jmap] vtc off, no call room may be
    projected at all. JmapExt::vtc already carries the switch; whatever
    runs at open must read it too.
  - A call room the agent has LEFT or that is inactive should not come
    back as a live VTCCall.
  - mediaTypes and subject are empty on a projection from the room, which
    is why the announcement of bead mimid-1wgh.114.1 carries them; a
    restored call has the same gap and the same answer.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW. It is the blocker for the JMAP-visible half of bead
mimid-1wgh.129. That bead's recovery is built and works -- a restart
loses the epoch's media secret, and Agent::rekey moves the epoch so
every member derives a fresh one (crates/mimid-agent-core/tests/
call_rooms.rs a_rekey_gives_the_call_a_media_secret_again) -- but a JMAP
client cannot reach it, because it cannot name the call. An embedder of
mimid-agent-core (purple-mimi, the mobile app of decision mimid-1wgh.39)
can, since it holds its own call state.

It also matters on its own: a client that reconnects after an agent
upgrade sees no calls, and has no way to tell "no call is running" from
"the agent forgot".

{"notes":"DONE 2026-11-25. A call survives a restart, under the id the client holds.

HOW, and it is not what this bead guessed. The bead said the smaller fix
was probably to re-project call rooms at open. That is wrong, and the
test that would have passed on it hid the reason: for a call this agent
HOSTED, project_call_room's id is the room's store key, while the id the
client holds was minted by VTCCall/set. Re-projecting gives the client a
call it cannot name, with mediaTypes and subject empty. So the record
keeps the whole VTCCall in the call room's ext["jmap"] -- the one place
where an object is kept whole rather than as what the record does not
render -- and the client's id, media kinds and subject all survive.
A record with no kept object (an older store, or one written while JMAP
was off) still falls back to the projection, now Render::new_call, so an
upgrade degrades rather than losing the call.

WHERE IT RUNS, and why not in over()/persisted(). crate-jmap's
MemoryBackend::seed_object whitelists the ten chat type names and panics
on anything else, so a VTCCall has to go in through the logged create,
which is async, where the chat types are seeded synchronously. It is
therefore AgentChat::restore_calls, awaited by Daemon::start right after
AgentChat::over. The rustdoc on over() and persisted() says in bold that
an embedder with [jmap] vtc on must await it. Nothing was written to
crate-jmap.

THE BLOCKER THIS FOUND, and it is a bug on main, not in this work:
STARTING A CALL MADE TWO VTCCalls. Store::start_call records the call's
own room before it returns, and create_call could only set mimiRoomId
afterwards, so any save in that window projected a second call for the
room -- under the room's key, with empty mediaTypes. The save that does
it is the runner's, on its own task (send_message only calls
want_sync()), so reordering the writes inside create_call narrowed the
window and did not close it: the duplicate still appeared in 3 of 3
runs. A client that started a call saw two calls in one room. Closed by
claiming the room's key before the room exists and releasing it when the
call names the room (vtc_backend::Starting, checked in
project_call_room). In scope here because the restoration cannot work
while two objects fight over one record's ext.

THE THREE CHECKS THIS BEAD LISTED:

* Decision mimid-1wgh.119 holds: restore_calls returns at once with the
  surface off, and keep_objects leaves a stored call ALONE rather than
  rewriting it, so a run with calls off (an IRC-only run) is not
  destructive. Test: a_run_with_the_surface_off_does_not_lose_the_call.
* A call room the user has left is not restored, and its stored object
  is dropped at the next save. Test:
  a_call_room_the_user_has_left_is_not_restored, which asserts BOTH
  halves (one call back, not two, not none) because either alone passes
  on a wrong implementation.
* mediaTypes and subject: no longer a gap for a call this agent hosted,
  because the object is kept. Still a gap for one projected from the
  room, with the same answer (the announcement of mimid-1wgh.114.1),
  recorded in Render::new_call's limitations.

A CALL IT CANNOT PUT BACK IS SKIPPED AND COUNTED, never an error. The
first version of restore_calls returned PersistError::Malformed, which
means the DAEMON DOES NOT START: one stale row of a call nobody is in
would cost the user every chat they have. It is reachable, not
hypothetical -- a store written before decision mimid-1wgh.120 was
corrected (bead mimid-1wgh.121) keeps a CHAT for its call room, which
will never deserialize as a VTCCall. Proven by the test below, which
failed with "the call of room ...: missing field `id`" from
Daemon::start before the change.

TESTS, in crates/mimid-agent/tests/vtc.rs: all five red first against
the source as it was before each of them.

* a_call_survives_a_restart_and_comes_back_at_a_new_epoch -- this bead
  and mimid-1wgh.129 together, replacing
  a_call_does_not_survive_a_restart_yet.
* starting_a_call_makes_one_and_the_record_keeps_it -- the duplicate.
  Its record half is the deterministic one; the /get half catches the
  race, and did so 3 times in 3 with the claim removed.
* a_run_with_the_surface_off_does_not_lose_the_call
* a_call_room_the_user_has_left_is_not_restored
* a_stored_call_that_is_not_a_call_does_not_stop_the_agent -- the skip,
  and with it the only coverage of the Render::new_call fallback: the
  second call room in that test keeps nothing and comes back projected
  from the room, which is what a store from between mimid-1wgh.121 and
  this bead looks like."}

new_value: {"notes":"SUPERSEDED 2026-11-25, the same day it shipped. Mark asked whether the call work was overengineered and then removed the projection layer this bead extended: a VTCCall is now DERIVED from its room on every read rather than stored, so there is no restoring to do. restore_calls, call_object, live_call_room, the keep_objects branch and the whole-object ext[\"jmap\"] persistence are gone, as is the Starting claim this bead's duplicate-call bug needed.\n\nWhat this bead found is still true and still matters, which is why the record is worth keeping: a call's id was minted by VTCCall/set on the hosting side and derived from the room key on the receiving side, and that single mismatch is what forced every mechanism in the layer. Making the id always the room's key is what let the layer go."}
